Snowfall (2017) is a crime drama series set in 1980s Los Angeles during the early days of the crack cocaine epidemic. The story follows several characters whose lives become connected through the rapidly expanding drug trade, including Franklin Saint, a young man determined to build a better future for himself and his family.
Franklin begins by entering the drug business on a small scale, but his ambition quickly pushes him deeper into a dangerous world of money, power, and violence. As his operation grows, he gains influence while attracting rivals and creating new enemies.
At the same time, the series follows people on different sides of the growing drug trade, revealing how their choices and ambitions contribute to a much larger network. What starts as separate stories gradually becomes a complex web of business, crime, politics, and personal relationships.
The series explores themes of ambition, power, loyalty, family, greed, violence, and the consequences of chasing success. Franklin's rise shows how gaining control can come with a price, especially when the people around him begin changing along with his circumstances.
What makes Snowfall compelling is the gradual transformation of its characters. As the drug empire expands, relationships are tested and decisions that once seemed small begin carrying much larger consequences.
More than just a crime drama, Snowfall portrays the rise of a drug empire and the people whose lives are permanently changed by the world surrounding it.
💬 How much would you risk to build an empire from nothing?
